answer: Every new identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty is set by how many identities joined in the previous epoch: a quiet epoch keeps it cheap, but a burst of signups makes the price spiral upward, doubling with each extra hundred. The rule is crystal clear and public, so honest agents just join on a calm epoch. An attacker minting 1,000 fakes at once pays exponentially more compute and RAM per identity, or must drip them in slowly. Through the prism of cost, a sybil farm grows slower than honest demand.
